headline: ESMA details CSRD enforcement priorities as EU maintains battery targets
summary: ESMA and national regulators have highlighted double materiality and negative impact disclosure as primary enforcement priorities for upcoming CSRD statements. Meanwhile, the EU reaffirmed its battery recycling targets, and member states continue implementing right-to-repair rules. Listed importers must ensure supply chain impact data is audit-ready.

items.title: ESMA publishes 2026 CSRD reporting enforcement priorities
items.what: ESMA set 2026 enforcement priorities for CSRD reporting, targeting double materiality, connectivity, and risk disclosures. Regulators like France's AMF highlighted the recommendations, explicitly warning listed companies against underreporting negative sustainability impacts.
items.meaning: As a listed importer within CSRD scope, your reporting will face scrutiny regarding negative environmental and social impacts across your Chinese supplier network.
items.action: Ensure your double materiality assessment thoroughly documents negative supplier impacts and aligns with financial disclosures.

items.title: EU confirms commitment to battery recycling targets
items.what: EU institutions reaffirmed their commitment to current battery recycling targets and waste rules under the EU Batteries Regulation, maintaining established circular economy expectations.
items.meaning: Compliance timelines for your proprietary battery platform remain firm, requiring verified supplier data on material recovery, recycled content, and collection performance.
items.action: Audit Chinese battery cell suppliers to confirm readiness for material recovery and recycled content documentation.

items.title: Member states advance right-to-repair implementation
items.what: EU member states are advancing right-to-repair provisions. Belgium launched a consumer repairer platform, while Spain reported delays transposing rules that extend warranties when consumers choose repair over replacement.
items.meaning: As the legal manufacturer of consumer power tools, national rollouts will govern your obligations regarding spare parts availability, repair access, and warranty obligations.
items.action: Assess spare parts availability and repair documentation across your primary EU consumer distribution networks.
